newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels say 100 soldiers killed in attack.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels say 100 soldiers killed in attack.

text.p: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels said they killed more than 100 Sri Lankan soldiers when they attacked troops near the government-held front-line town of Vavuniya on Tuesday.

The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio claimed the rebels had also destroyed five army tanks and damaged a helicopter gunship when they hit the army's forward defence line near Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.

The Defence Ministry said earlier in a statement that more than 500 rebels had tried to dislodge the army's field headquarters and artillery positions at Thandikulam, near Vavuniya, in order to disrupt a government offensive.

The statement said the LTTE, which has been fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of mostly Sinhalese Sri Lanka since 1983, launched the attack in a bid to cut off supplies to troops fighting further north.
"But troops fought back valiantly to repulse the attack, causing very heavy casualties among the terrorists," it said.
LTTE radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said that about 50 rebels had also been killed during the attack.
The radio claimed that the rebels were still in control of Thandikulam after more than a day's fighting.
Defence Ministry spokesmen were not immediately available for comment on the rebel version of the battle.
Military officials in the north earlier said at least 34 Tamil Tiger rebels and seven government soldiers were killed in the attack.
Three soldiers, two sailors and two special forces troopers were killed, while more than 27 soldiers were wounded, military officials said.
An aid worker in Vavuniya told Reuters that three civilians, including a seven-year-old girl, had been killed in the fighting. Some 28 people were wounded and admitted to Vavuniya hospital, he added.
The rebels warned that surprise attacks like the one on Tuesday could take place more often.
"The Sri Lanka army can expect many more military disasters like this in coming weeks," LTTE's international spokesman, Anton Rajah, told Reuters from London.

Military officials said the rebels blew up a key bridge at Nochchimoddai, just north of Thandikulam, from where security forces had launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on the rebels' Wanni stronghold nearly one month ago.
An ammunition dump was destroyed when a rebel mortar round hit it, the ministry statement said.
Mi-24 helicopter gunships and Pucara ground-attack planes fired at the rebels from the air, causing them to flee into nearby jungle, the officials said.
LTTE radio said the rebels had fired 30 artillery rounds at the army and air force bases in Vavuniya. Military officials said they caused little damage.
A Defence Ministry spokesman said earlier on Tuesday the attack would not be a setback to troops who had already captured several rebel-held towns in the Wanni, driving the LTTE further north.

He said the military would take full control of the area by Tuesday evening, allowing troops to carry on with the offensive. "We have enough troops to guard the rear and advance at the same time," he said.
But residents in Vavuniya said they could hear artillery shells exploding to the north at 5 p.m. (1100 GMT), which meant fighting was still continuing at Thandikulam.
"It's going to be a long night for us," one resident said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
